close_reason: Bikeshedding — '## [1.0.0] — TBD' was deliberately rolled out across all 12 1.0-scope crates in commit 362979de (PKIX-wlsr.7.2). The pattern is a workspace convention with the date filled at publish time. Retracting the finding.
description:
CHANGELOG.md:11: '## [1.0.0] — TBD'. The section then enumerates every feature, including the async traits and cache, as 'Added' in 1.0.0. This pattern (consolidate all pre-1.0 work into the eventual 1.0.0 section) is reasonable for a workspace doing a 1.0 cut, but readers landing on the changelog before 1.0.0 ships see a future-dated release with 'Added' items that are TODAY in the code.

The current shape conflates two things: (a) what's in HEAD, and (b) what 1.0.0 will contain when it eventually ships. Pre-1.0 readers conventionally want (a); post-1.0 readers want (b). The crate's [Unreleased] section being empty while [1.0.0]—TBD has everything inverts the convention.

Either (a) keep [Unreleased] as the bucket for pending changes and move them to 1.0.0 at release-cut, or (b) document the convention so consumers seeing this don't get confused. Workspace-wide consistency matters here — looking at the workspace CHANGELOG.md should clarify the pattern.
title: CHANGELOG [1.0.0] section uses 'TBD' as version date but lists every feature as added
